An estimate is one outcome. Precision is a distribution.

A new estimate

01 · THE INTUITION
Nearby worlds are hard to tell apart.
Information measures how sensitively the data distribution changes when the parameter moves.
Same separation · different noise
Data densities; not posterior probabilities.
A change must leave a trace.
Almost indistinguishable data cannot support arbitrarily concentrated, locally unbiased estimates.
More Fisher information permits a lower variance bound.

02 · THE MECHANISM
Likelihood → score → Fisher information.
The likelihood is a function of the candidate parameter, with the observed dataset held fixed.
1 · Likelihood
A likelihood is not a probability density over θ.
2 · Score
Under regularity, the score has mean zero.
3 · Fisher information
Expected squared score = expected curvature, under the required interchange conditions.

02 · THE THEOREM
The scalar Cramér–Rao Bound.
A floor for the variance of locally unbiased estimators in a regular model.
The variance floor
Variance: squared units · SD: parameter units
The theorem has a scope.
Unbiasedness
Eθ[T] = θ in a neighborhood.
Regularity
Differentiate under the expectation; Eθ[Uθ] = 0.
Finite information
0 < Iₙ(θ) < ∞ and finite estimator variance.
Known model
The likelihood describes the experiment.

02 · WHY IT IS TRUE
One score identity. One Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.
An unbiased estimator must move, on average, at the same rate as the true parameter.
The score identity
1 Differentiate unbiasedness
2 Move the derivative inside
3 Use the zero-mean score
Cauchy–Schwarz
An unbiased estimator must respond to the score.

04 · ATTAINABILITY
“Lower bound” does not mean “always achievable.”
Equality requires a very specific relationship between the estimator and the score.
Equality in Cauchy–Schwarz
The same statistic must work throughout the parameter range.
Keep three claims distinct.
Unbiased
Expectation equals the target.
Efficient
Variance attains the CRB.
Maximum likelihood
Maximizes likelihood; finite-sample bias is possible.
Regular MLEs may attain the bound asymptotically.

05 · LAB 3 · PREDICT FIRST
Same sensors. Different geometry. Different limits.
Four accurate ranges can still leave one position direction poorly constrained.
Predict the weak direction
Surround
Anchors point toward the target from different directions.
Cluster
Anchors share almost the same line of sight.
Collinear
Anchors and target lie on the same straight line.
Position error bound
For an unbiased position estimator:
Euclidean RMSE ≥ PEB.
Finite local information does not rule out distant mirror solutions.

06 · WHEN THE USUAL FORMULA FAILS
A moving support breaks the familiar proof.
Not every model allows differentiation to pass through the expectation.
Xi ∼ Uniform(0, θ)
The moving boundary invalidates the regular score identity.
Check the estimator directly.
The variance follows from the distribution of the sample maximum.

07 · USE THE BOUND
Design the experiment, not only the estimator.
A new independent, correctly modeled measurement adds a positive-semidefinite information term.
Linear Gaussian measurements
H sets sensitivity and geometry.
R sets noise and correlation.
Choose a design objective
Total variance
Minimize tr(J⁻¹)
Ellipsoid volume
Maximize log det J
Weakest direction
Maximize λmin(J)
Local criteria depend on the parameterization and units.

07 · INTERPRETATION
Read a CRB result like a careful reviewer.
Before comparing an algorithm with a bound, make sure they solve the same statistical problem.
01 · Estimator class
Is the comparison valid?
Analyze bias before comparing a learned, constrained, or regularized estimator with an unbiased bound.
02 · Parameter vector
What was treated as known?
Include unknown offsets, calibration, orientation, and other nuisance parameters before inverting.
03 · Metric and model
Are the assumptions aligned?
Match variance, MSE, and RMSE with the correct bound. Model measurement correlations.
04 · Local versus global
What can the bound miss?
Inspect rank, conditioning, competing solutions, and low-information regimes.

08 · TAKEAWAYS
Three ideas to keep.
More information lowers the bound. Bias changes the comparison. Geometry decides the weak directions.
01 · Sensitivity
Information belongs to the experiment.
Noise and sensing design change the limits before any estimator runs.
02 · Precision
Unbiased variance has a floor.
An estimator within the theorem’s class cannot beat the floor.
03 · Direction
The matrix tells you where.
Complementary measurement directions improve the weakest constraints.
